title: Improve NCCL overlap and scheduling for tensor-parallel collectives
author: Amelia Chen
description:
Motivation: tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads in the serving runtime are increasingly hitting NCCL collective overheads and stream contention, which reduces effective overlap between communication and compute and increases tail latency. This PR implements runtime-side scheduling and NCCL tuning changes to improve overlap, reduce synchronization points, and pick better collective algorithms for common sequence-length / batch-size regimes.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a dedicated per-collective CUDA stream model: each tensor-parallel collective (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter) is issued on an NCCL stream bound to a dedicated CUDA stream with adjustable priority so that compute kernels can be scheduled on separate streams to enable true overlap.
- Adds explicit cudaEvent-based sync points and lightweight dependency tracking in the TP scheduler to avoid unnecessary device-wide synchronizations. We now only block compute when data dependencies require it (KV cache updates, embedding writes), otherwise compute continues while collectives progress.
- Exposes NCCL algorithm and ring/tree heuristic based on size heuristics and topology: small messages favor tree algorithms for latency, large messages use ring for bandwidth. Heuristics derived from microbench results included here.
- Implements batched collective grouping using ncclGroupStart()/ncclGroupEnd() where possible to reduce kernel launch overhead and allow NCCL internal scheduling to better pipeline multiple collectives.
- Optimizes buffer lifecycle: use pinned staging buffers for cross-device memcpy, reduce unnecessary cudaMemcpySync calls, and reuse per-request pinned buffers from a pool to reduce allocation overhead.
- Adds a scheduling optimization that delays low-impact collectives (KV prefix fetch merges) by a few microseconds to batch them with upcoming collectives when throughput benefits outweigh latency. This is tunable by runtime flags.

Changes in the codebase (files touched):
- runtime/tensor_parallel/nccl_manager.cpp: new stream/priority management, heuristics for algorithm selection, grouping logic.
- runtime/tensor_parallel/nccl_manager.h: exported flags + tuning knobs.
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cc: dependency tracking updates, event-based sync, and delayed-collective batching hooks.
- runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cpp: reduced sync when applying KV cache updates; moved writes to lower-priority stream when safe.
- runtime/utils/pinned_pool.cc/h: pinned buffer pool implementation and plumbing.
- tests/perf/tp_nccl_overlap_bench.py: microbench harness and new scenarios (varied seq len / micro-batches).
- scripts/ci/tune_matrix.yml: adds a perf job to track TP overlap regressions.

Performance results (microbench):
- End-to-end TP throughput improved by ~18% for long sequences (2k tokens) in our 8-GPU p4d-like cluster profile.
- P99 per-request latency decreased by ~22% under realistic bursty traffic in the canary bench.
- GPU compute utilization increased 10-15% due to reduced blocking.
- Small-message latency improved ~12% due to tree-algo heuristic.

Testing and validation:
- Added unit tests for the pinned buffer pool and scheduler dependency tracking.
- Added integration microbench scenarios in tests/perf to reproduce overlap improvements.
- Ran CI perf job on a representative cluster: initial runs surfaced a flaky ordering issue in cudaEvent handling (fixed by adding explicit event destruction and stronger ordering assertions).
- Stress tested on internal perf-canary harness across 4/8/16 GPU shapes; no regressions observed for CPU/IO-bound paths.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- All new behaviors are behind runtime flags (env vars) and default to the previous behavior for safety. The default heuristic set is enabled in canary for controlled rollouts.
- No user-facing API changes. Not a breaking change.

Ops notes / config knobs:
- TP_NCCL_ENABLE_STREAM_PRIORITY (bool): enable per-collective stream priority usage.
- TP_NCCL_ALGO_HEURISTICS (json string): serialized heuristics mapping sizes -> algo; can be overridden in cluster config.
- TP_DELAYED_BATCH_MICROS (int): microsecond window to batch low-impact collectives.

Related work and references:
- Internal dev ticket ENG-4921: perf regression on 8-GPU TP serving.
- ENG-4972: KV cache contention under high concurrency.
- Prior PRs: pr-18742, pr-19512, pr-21023 that iterated on NCCL overlap in different hotspots.

Release notes: "Improved tensor-parallel multi-GPU runtime: better overlap between NCCL collectives and compute, improved throughput and lower tail latency via NCCL algorithm heuristics, stream priority, and pinned buffer reuse."

Risks and follow-ups:
- Some topologies (mixed PCIe/NVLink) show different optimal heuristics; follow-up will add topology-aware tuning.
- We observed a rare deadlock in internal stress when combining delayed batching + non-blocking KV writes; mitigated with additional safety checks but will monitor in canary.
- Follow-up tasks: add telemetry (per-collective durations, wait times) to Redwood Console to make knob tuning easier (ENG-5060).

scheduler: add event-based dependency tracking and delayed collective batching
kv_cache: avoid device-wide sync for safe writes
utils: pinned buffer pool with reuse
tests: perf harness and unit tests for new components
ci: add perf job to detect regressions
